title: The Business of Persuasion
text:
Advertising companies spend billions of dollars every year to persuade consumers to buy products. Many of them rely on celebrities, because viewers tend to trust people they admire. Digital platforms have made this process more precise, since algorithms can show an advertisement to people whose recent searches suggest an interest in a product.

However, critics argue that such targeting can be intrusive and may encourage people to spend money they do not need. Some governments have therefore introduced rules requiring advertisers to label sponsored content clearly. Supporters of these rules believe that transparency helps audiences make more informed decisions.

questions.text: According to paragraph one, why do advertisers often use celebrities?
options: Because viewers tend to trust people they admire
Because celebrities are cheaper than ordinary actors
Because celebrities never appear in digital media
Because algorithms require a famous face

questions.text: What have some governments introduced, according to paragraph two?
options: Rules requiring advertisers to label sponsored content clearly
A limit on the number of digital platforms

questions.text: What can be inferred about digital advertising from the passage?
options: It is less effective than traditional advertising
It can target people more precisely based on their behaviour
It is mostly regulated by governments
It never raises concerns among critics

questions.text: Why might critics be concerned about personalised targeting?
options: It makes advertisements too short to notice
It may lead people to spend money they do not need
It reduces the number of products on sale
It prevents celebrities from earning money

vocabulary.definition: to make someone do or believe something by giving reasons or encouragement
interfering in someone's private life in an unwelcome way
the quality of being open and easy to understand
paid for by a company in return for promotion

paragraph_translations: Firmy reklamowe co roku wydają miliardy dolarów, aby przekonać konsumentów do zakupu produktów. Wiele z nich korzysta z gwiazd, ponieważ widzowie chętniej ufają osobom, które podziwiają. Platformy cyfrowe sprawiły, że proces ten jest bardziej precyzyjny, ponieważ algorytmy mogą pokazać reklamę osobom, których ostatnie wyszukiwania sugerują zainteresowanie produktem.

Krytycy twierdzą jednak, że takie ukierunkowanie może być natrętne i zachęcać ludzi do wydawania pieniędzy, których nie potrzebują. Niektóre rządy wprowadziły zatem przepisy wymagające wyraźnego oznaczania treści sponsorowanych. Zwolennicy tych przepisów uważają, że przejrzystość pomaga odbiorcom podejmować lepiej poinformowane decyzje.
